sections.html:
Halifax County runs along the North Carolina border, and the town of Halifax is the county seat. South Boston is the largest town, and the other incorporated towns are Scottsburg and Virgilina. The county covers 830 square miles, of which 818 are land. U.S. 58, U.S. 360 and U.S. 501 cross it, and census-designated places include Clover, Cluster Springs, Mountain Road, Nathalie and Riverdale.

Population peaked at 41,442 in the 1950 census and has fallen since. It was 37,355 in 2000, 34,022 in 2020 and an estimated 33,447 in 2025. The county has 17,275 housing units, 14.9% of them vacant in 2020, and 70.8% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.

Older owners, a shrinking population and many empty houses tend to produce estate sales and neglected properties. If you inherited a Halifax County house that you will not keep, the tax bill still arrives every year.

sections.h2: An old record trap: South Boston
sections.html: South Boston was an independent city through the 1990 census, then reverted to a town and rejoined Halifax County in 1995. A seller whose papers mention the city of South Boston should ask the Commissioner of the Revenue which office holds the parcel today.

sections.h2: Treasurer and Commissioner of the Revenue
sections.html:
The Treasurer collects. The Commissioner of the Revenue is the chief tax authority and keeps the real estate ownership records. Both offices share an address, 1030 Mary Bethune Street in Halifax.

  • Treasurer: Suite 103, phone 434-476-3318, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Commissioner of the Revenue: Suite 104, phone 434-476-3314, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Card payments carry a 2.50% convenience charge with a $2.00 minimum, and eCheck payments cost a flat $1.50. The Clerk of the Circuit Court records the deed when a house sells.

Tax type2026 rate
Real estate$0.50 per $100 of value
Personal property$3.85 per $100
Machinery and tools$1.26 per $100

Real estate tax is due June 5 and December 5. Personal property and machinery and tools tax are due December 5. A year with a late rate vote can shift the first date, so check the Treasurer's notice if your June bill is slow to arrive.

The Treasurer also posts a list titled Sale of Valuable Real Estate each fall. If your parcel number appears on it, call the Treasurer the same day.

sections.h2: Tax relief for elderly and disabled owners
sections.html:
The Real Estate Tax Relief Program discounts the bill for owners who are elderly or permanently disabled and meet income and net worth tests. The discount covers the house and up to one acre of land.

  • The applicant must be 65 or permanently and totally disabled on December 31 of the prior year.
  • The applicant must own and live in the home on that date.
  • Gross combined income can be no more than $22,000, and income of relatives living in the house counts above $8,500.
  • Net worth can be no more than $60,000, not counting the house and one acre.

Limits can change, so confirm them with the Commissioner before you rely on them. The same office has forms for a disabled former service member exemption and for a land use program.

The Commissioner's page carries a 2026 Real Estate Assessment Appeal Application, so start with that form. Virginia law also lets a person assessed by a commissioner of the revenue ask for a correction. The request must come within three years of the end of the tax year or one year from the assessment date, whichever is later, and it applies when the error was the commissioner's or came from a factual mistake in a general reassessment.

Bring photographs, repair bids and recent sales of similar houses. A correction is easier to win when the mistake is plain, such as wrong acreage or a building that no longer stands.

sections.h2: When the house sells with tax owing
sections.html:
Under the Code of Virginia the real estate tax lien comes before every other lien and lasts until the taxing authority is paid. A purchaser or foreclosure trustee must send sale money toward the taxes, and penalties and interest count as taxes. At a normal closing the title company asks the Treasurer for a payoff and pays it from the seller's proceeds.

  1. Ask the Treasurer for the balance in writing.
  2. Find out whether the second half is already billed.
  3. Give the figure to the title company.
  4. Check afterward that the account shows paid.

sections.h2: Preparing a Halifax County house for sale
sections.html:
Typical sellers here have an inherited farmhouse, a rental with tenants, a vacant house in one of the smaller towns, or a house that needs repairs. With 14.9% of housing units vacant in 2020, empty homes are a normal part of the market, and a buyer will compare yours with several of them.

Collect the latest tax bill, the parcel number, every name on the deed and any relief or land use paperwork. If the owner has died, tell the title company early, since the person acting for the estate needs documented authority to sign. A cash sale skips showings, repair bargaining and a buyer's loan approval. Cash Home Buyers purchases Halifax County houses as they are, and unpaid real estate tax is paid from the proceeds at closing. Ask for a written payoff first, so you can weigh any offer against what you would keep.

faqs.q: What is the Halifax County real estate tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The Treasurer lists $0.50 per $100 of value for real estate in 2026.

faqs.q: When are Halifax County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. Personal property and machinery and tools are due December 5.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Halifax County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Commissioner of the Revenue at 434-476-3314. Call the Treasurer at 434-476-3318 for balances and payments.

faqs.q: Does Halifax County offer tax relief for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. A program covers owners 65 or older or permanently disabled who meet income and net worth limits, and it applies to the house and up to one acre.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Halifax County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so request a payoff from the Treasurer before the closing date.
